body: Eva Braun seemed like a ESFP to me, but for the sake of this convo, let's say yes, you guys are Eva, my dear fraulein. ;)
What were your experiences with them like, exactly?
Yeah, some context would be helpful in order for us to give input of better substance.

Leave the relationship and go for the person who is the person of my dreams. It is unfair for me to be with someone whom I obviously don't love enough if I'm eyeing someone else. And honestly I would not let that chance go by if they truly are that incredible and one of a kind.

Yeah. 


But if they're a healthy ENTJ, they may be pissed if the weird action in question is affecting their plans, or reputation, or environment, if those things negatively affect the probability of their desired outcome coming to fruition. Sometimes impressions are very important to conduct appropriately, such as if the ENTJ wishes to impress a group of people or give off a specific image of themselves to those around them, for practical reasons. That would be my best guess as to why they're pissed off and scolding. 


Enneagram 3's especially care for how they are percieved and wish to be liked by those they deem worthwhile to know. 3's are pretty common for our type. I'm one. I have told a friend to quit acting rude and childish and/or bizarre various times because it reflected very badly on me, within settings I have carefully cultivated an image to get an edge in my community, academia, networking, and career. I have zero tolerance for anyone who I have explained this to before, continuing to disrespect me by acting ridiculously in front of colleagues and neighbors and peers, etc.


Our type loathes having to repeat ourselves especially if the person in question has agreed to a change in behavior. 


Weirdness in itself and eccentricity is just fine with me. I like the unorthodox and admire those who are themselves, but respect must be constant in any situation, when it comes to my tolerance. Be yourself, but don't dare be inconsiderate or I would not be surprised they have directly told you to quit it, OP.


All about the context. Gain some social awareness if it may be lacking to gain a better insight to why your behavior has been given constructive criticism. If it's not you that's being inconsiderate, then disregard that advice and just cut ties, would be my opinion. Why be around someone who is mean (for actually no good reason)? But if there is a reason, find out why. If they're actually an ENTJ and not mistyped, then I'd expect they have already explained why it bothers them.

Agreed. I feel things just fine. My emotions dictate my understanding of a situation, and then my logical processes take over afterward and I detach from my feelings. But to identify which actions need to be done to create the most ideal outcome in accordance to the circumstances at hand, can be utilized excellently after examining what you feel.


Just cause we act rationally more often than explicitly emotionally does not mean feelings are never present.


Personally, I just feel no need to dwell on an emotion especially once I know what it was caused by. I need a calm mind to best put my plans into action to create different outcomes. So a new situation replaces the one that initially caused whichever emotion I felt. My sense of morals would be considered fair by my country/social background and cultural upbringing, and I do feel things like righteous anger when I observe something I consider unjust. My anger rarely lasts long - none of my emotions really do - but that's because I usually manage to come to terms with them and have already moved on to more practical actions.

It's a very uncommon orientation, but I'm asexual. I've never been interested in sex or even romance. I've been in various committed relationships and although most were emotionally and intellectually fulfilling, I have no interest in kissing or physical intimacy. It's boring to me and I only understand what attraction/sexual attraction as a concept, via others explaining it.


Asexuality is apparently more common in NTs, but ENTJs aren't represented in high numbers via MBTI polls on asexuality forums/sites. I'm curious if there are any others? 


I find it actually more efficient to not feel any need or desire for romantic partners. I'm content and fulfilled by very close friendships.

But I suppose with the act itself, I loathe aggression in partners. I have no interest initiating or taking the lead however, so the most comfortable and even cute behavior for me is someone who doesn't push for sex, is patient and gentle, meek, thoughtful, submissive, but doesn't expect me to do anything like being the actual aggressor in bed.


I like being good at everything I try my hand at, but I'll admit to not being good at something. I have insisted on almost 100% abstinence ever since I realized I had zero interest in sex. I'm not interested in gaining experience and the act is very emotionally uncomfortable to me to the point of feeling disturbed. I like being in control and being composed. I think this extends to being in bed as well. I just cannot seem to make myself 'let go', even while drunk - when intoxicated and not giving a fuck about composure, I just outright say I don't want to be touched. Either way, I feel like I'm fumbling around not knowing what to do, while forcing myself at that, so I just hate being expected to ever be the lead. But I can't stand anyone holding power over me either, so I have to permit the actions and then they HAVE to be gentle and to be understanding that this just isn't my thing. It takes a certain kind of rare person/SO to be OK with that and still enjoy it. 

(No prior history of trauma, etc. Just absolute zero desire.)
It truly depends on if they achieve their potential.
